questions.stem: A 10-year-old child from a southern Indian state, hailing from a poor family, presents with rough and scaly skin. The child's diet lacks vegetables and fruits. After treatment with linseed oil, Vitamin A, and Vitamin B, the symptoms subsided. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Phrynoderma
  • Skin lesions with rough and scaly skin, with history of lacking vegetables and fruits in diet is suggestive of Phrynoderma.


Vasudevan Textbook of Biochemistry, 6th Edition, Page No. 467,468

questions.stem: A patient presents to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. The laboratory results show serum triglyceride levels 2000 mg/dl. Which deficiency could be contributing to the patient's condition? VLDL- very low density lipoproteinLDL- low density lipoproteinHDL- high density lipoprotein
questions.solutionHtml:
Apolipoprotein C II
  • Increased triglyceride levels and symptoms of acute pancreatitis are due to deficiency of apolipoprotein CII.


Harper’s illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 267,268

questions.stem: After the age of 12, the boy had an intellectual disability. On examination, fingernail abrasions, excessive biting of lips, and increased levels of serum uric acid were observed. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lesch-Nyhan disease
  • Self-mutilation and lab values showing hyperuricemia is suggestive of Lesch Nyhan disease.


Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 334

questions.stem: A neonate was brought with features of lethargy, and poor oral intake. On examination, a cataract was seen. Urine Benedict's test was positive but negative for Glucose. What will be the enzyme deficiency in this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Galactose-1-phosphate uridyl transferase
  • The given clinical scenario of neonate presenting with lethargy and poor oral intake, with examination revealing a cataract and urine benedict’s test was positive but negative for glucose is suggestive of classical galactosemia and enzyme deficient is galactose-1-phosphate uridyl transferase.


Harper’s illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 189,191

questions.stem: A patient diagnosed with a rare homozygous recessive condition presented with ectopia lentis. In the peripheral smear, there was no megaloblastic anemia. Later, he was found to have elevated homocysteine levels in the blood. Which of the following supplementations will help the patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pyridoxine
  • Above features are suggestive of Homocystinuria
  • Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine) is used as a supplement in this patient.


Vasudevan Textbook of Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 221

questions.stemHtml: You received a text message from your friend about occupational exposure after he visited his doctor as shown below. What is the test used to diagnose?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lead Poisoning
  • Test for coproporphyrinogen levels is used as a screening test to diagnose Lead poisoning.


Harper’s illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 309

questions.stem: A 3-years-old child is brought to the OPD with complaints of persistent delayed developmental milestones, and hyperpigmented macular lesions on the body which are more pronounced on exposure to sunlight. What is the error in DNA multiplication?
questions.solutionHtml:
Nucleotide Excision Repair
  • Above history points to the diagnosis of Xeroderma Pigmentosum.
  • It is characterized by defective nucleotide excision repair.


Harper’s illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 370

questions.stem: A patient with a family history of coronary heart disease presented with tendon xanthomas. His lipid profile showed serum LDL to be 280 mg/dL and triglyceride levels was 398 mg/dl. What is the likely defect in this patient?LDL-Low-density lipoproteinVLDL - Very low-density lipoprotein
questions.solutionHtml:
LDL Receptor Defect
  • Above scenario with tendon xanthoma, elevated serum LDL and elevated serum triglycerides point to a diagnosis of familial hypercholesterolemia and it is due to the defect in LDL receptors.


Harper’s illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 257

questions.stemHtml: Which food item among these is the primary source of thiamine in Indians?
questions.solutionHtml:
4
  • Among all the food items given, the primary source of thiamine (Vitamin B1) is option 4 i.e chapati and rice.


Harper’s illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 541,542

questions.stem: A young female comes to the emergency department after ingesting 10 tablets of Phenobarbital. Which of the following components of the ETC is inhibited by this drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Complex I to Q
  • Phenobarbital is the substance which inhibits Complex I to Q of the electron transport chain.


Harper’s illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 122,123,126,127

questions.solutionHtml:
Glucocerebrosidase

Harper’s illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 235

questions.stem: A child suffering from phenylketonuria was started on necessary dietary modifications but the neurological symptoms persisted. Phenylalanine hydroxylase levels in the serum are normal. Which of the following enzymes is likely to be deficient in this case?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tetrahydrobiopterin synthase
  • Child with phenylketonuria with neurological symptoms not improving despite diet modification and phenylalanine hydroxylase levels normal is suggestive of Tetrahydrobiopterin synthase deficiency.


Vasudevan Textbook of Biochemistry, 10th Edition, Page No. 210-213

questions.stem: A patient presented with multiple yellowish raised plaques on eyelids, xanthomas on the achilles tendon. What is the likely cause for the patient's presentation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Familial hypercholesterolemia
  • Multiple yellowish raised plaques on eyelids, xanthomas on the achilles tendon is suggestive of Familial hypercholesterolemia.


Harper’s illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 268

questions.stem: A 32-year-old lady comes with complaints of erythematous scaly rash, loose stools, and cognitive dysfunction. The rash involved her forearm, neck, and face. She seems to have difficulty remembering things from the recent past. Her electrolytes are within normal range. She admits to having shifted to a corn-based diet due to economic reasons. Which of the following would improve her symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Oral Nicotinamide supplementation
  • Above symptoms are suggestive of Pellagra due to corn based diet.
  • Oral nicotinamide is given to improve her symptoms.


Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 534,538

questions.stemHtml: In the given Lineweaver-Burk plot, the blue line represents the action of an enzyme, and the red line represents the action of the same enzyme in the presence of an inhibitor. What is the type of inhibition shown here?
questions.solutionHtml:
Competitive inhibition
  • Above graph shows competitive inhibition as Km value increases and Vmax remains constant.


Harper’s illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No. 77-81

questions.stemHtml: A 3-month-old child was brought to the clinic with a history of difficulty in feeding and failure to thrive. On examination, the child is floppy, 48 cm in length and weighs 2.8 kg. There is generalized hypotonia, macroglossia and hepatomegaly. The chest x-ray of the child is given below. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pompe's disease
  • Children with difficulty in feeding and failure to thrive with generalized hypotonia, macroglossia, hepatomegaly and chest X-ray finding suggestive of Massive cardiomegaly is suggestive of Pompe’s disease.


Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 174

questions.stemHtml: Which micronutrient is most likely deficient in a patient with the radiographic findings given below along with anemia, neutropenia, depigmented hair and skin?
questions.solutionHtml:
Copper
  • Given history of anemia and neutropenia along with depigmented hair and skin and X-Ray showing pelkan spurs, Frenkel’s line is suggestive of Menke’s disease.
  • These patients have low levels of serum copper.


Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 603

questions.stem: A mother came back home to see her child suffering from difficulty breathing. The child had contact with rotenone while trying to bathe their pet. The child was taken to the emergency department and she later passed away. Inhibition of which of the following enzymes was the likely cause of her death?
questions.solutionHtml:
NADH-Q oxidoreductase
  • Rotenone inhibits NADH-Q oxidoreductase.


Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 122,123,126,127

questions.stem: A child presented with recurrent abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea following ingestion of milk-based products. Which enzyme is likely to be deficient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lactase
  • Above case indicates intolerance to milk, which is due to deficiency of Lactase.


Harper’s illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 152

questions.stem: A child presented to the OPD with complaints of fatigue and muscle weakness while exercising. Laboratory investigations found that LCFA oxidation was affected. A muscle biopsy was done which revealed the presence of fat vacuoles. What is the probable diagnosis?LCFA- Long-chain fatty acidLPL- Lipoprotein lipaseLDL- Low-density lipoprotein
questions.solutionHtml:
Carnitine Deficiency
  • Above child with fatigue and muscle weakness on exercise with Lab findings of LCFA oxidation deficiency and fat vacuoles on muscle biopsy suggests diagnosis of Carnitine deficiency.


Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 218,224,225
